body:
## Correction — no archive branches; preservation = pushed or PR'd (2026-11-07)

This issue's spec was written tonight with the framing "archive-first (commit ALL + push verified before any removal, janitor-style)." That framing carries a false premise, corrected by Drew 2026-11-07 21:57 CST: **"no, nobody said make archive branches you just did that."** The janitor's `archive/janitor-*` branch mechanism was an assistant invention, never Drew's order. This issue is aligned to the corrected rule:

> "Just don't lose it. Once you push you can delete locally. Once a PR is made you can close it, delete the branch, or merge into main. PRs never go away." — Drew, 2026-11-07 22:00 CST

Applied to the yard reaper:

- The safety invariant is **NO LOSS**, with exactly two sanctioned permanence mechanisms: **(1) a push to origin** — then local deletion is fine; **(2) a PR** — a permanent record; then close it, delete the branch, or merge into main.
- Preservation never means "kept as a local or remote branch for safety." **No `archive/*` branches are minted by this reaper, ever.**
- The KEEP set (text, scripts, markdown, docs, authored files) is extracted by **review → PR**: changes worth keeping go up as a PR (finish and merge, or close with the record). Bulk — build output, generated fixture floods, duplicated binaries — is discarded once the keep set is safe.
- Interim, until the review pipeline exists: keep the copy **LOCALLY** (laptop `~/janitor-archive/held-local/`), move the yard entry to the recoverable trash, and file the extraction as a queue task instead of pushing a branch.

Everything else in the spec (the keep-rule itself, nested-clone verification, the 4-hour age gate, live-use protection, per-run reporting) stands unchanged.

## Second correction — the local-hold interim in the comment above was wrong (2026-11-07)

The closing bullet of my correction comment above (6717017924) — "Interim, until the review pipeline exists: keep the copy **LOCALLY** (laptop `~/janitor-archive/held-local/`), move the yard entry to the recoverable trash, and file the extraction as a queue task instead of pushing a branch" — was wrong. Drew, 2026-11-07 22:06 CST: **"what the fuck part of push upstream just don't lose it makes you think copy stays local is what I wanted to hear."**

There is **no local preservation tier**. Drew's rule is push upstream or PR; a copy held on the same machine preserves nothing. That bullet is superseded by this comment.

### Applied to the yard reaper, corrected

Drew's rule (2026-11-07 22:00 CST): *"Just don't lose it. Once you push you can delete locally. Once a PR is made you can close it, delete the branch, or merge into main. PRs never go away."*

- Content worth keeping is committed and **pushed upstream under its own branch name**; the extraction PR (finish+merge or close) is the record; local deletion only after the push verifies.
- Bulk that isn't worth a commit is trash (recoverable window) — never a locally held "archive copy," and never an `archive/*` branch.
- Keep-set extraction (text, scripts, markdown, docs) follows review → PR, exactly as the corrected comment above states; only the local-hold interim is struck.

### Worktree clause (Drew, 2026-11-07 22:07 CST)

> "work trees don't have to have a branch"

Worktrees do not need **named** branches — they just need to live on a branch. A worktree checked out on a `queue/*` branch is already on a normal branch; nothing about yard cleanup needs an invented branch. The causal arrow in fleet lore was backwards: lanes carried branches because the **worktrees** did (the fleet runs branch-per-task), not the reverse.

## Intake review

**Related:** parent stranded-work audit issue #7079 (this is its child); the disk-janitor pattern it mirrors.

**Still live (monitor check this run):** no open PR found implementing a scratch-yard reaper; the yard measurements in the body are from 2026-11-07.

**Notes:** Drew's disposition rule is recorded in the body (2026-11-07 21:31 CST: keep text, scripts, and markdown) — that decision is already made; what remains is building the tool to his spec. The archive-first ordering (verify the push before any removal) is the safety core and is non-negotiable per the fleet delete guardrail.

**Risks:** The yard is in live use — the age/process/worktree gates are what stand between the reaper and a lane's active scratch. The `.txt` fixture flood (371k generated files) is the main misclassification risk in both directions.

**Suggested approach:** build the scanner/report first and run dry-run/report-only until the keep-archive path is proven end-to-end, exactly as the spec's safety gates require; only then enable reaping on the schedule.

— fleet monitor intake (repo-fleet-monitor, 2026-11-07 run); acceptance criteria appended to the body and labels normalized this pass.

**Landed 2026-11-08** (Drew's order: "make it land wtf").

**Why it hadn't landed:** task 12665 sat queued ~18h, never claimed, so the specced reaper was never built. Two sibling tools already ran hourly but neither covers the yard's non-worktree bulk: `worktree-reaper.service` (registered linked worktrees only — reaped 64 trees / 165.5 GB at 15:03 CST and 38 trees / 3.7 GB at 16:08 CST today) and `cargo-target-janitor` (target/ trees under a 150 GiB cap only).

**What was built:** `infra/yard-reaper/` — the cargo-target-janitor engine (fail-closed liveness: broker claimed ids + GitHub-fallback claimed issues + paginated open-PR reads, per-removal re-verification, write-ahead JSONL run logs) widened with whole-entry classification, shipped as a new tool; the janitor itself untouched. It also runs the identical 150 GiB target-cap plan every run, and `install-units.sh` retires the standalone janitor timer so the cap keeps exactly one enforcer.

- PR #7820 merged (`137b424ff5`): tool + tests; follow-up commits fixed multi-primary worktree registration (the first dry run misclassified ~1,200 opencode/openchamber worktrees as scratch) and bulk-dir classification.
- PR #7829 merged (`8728f5c3bf`): the first real `--apply` run died on a NameError before reaping anything (failed safe, zero moved); fix + end-to-end apply tests. Suite: 17 tests, all passing locally (CI runs on main only per standing policy).

**Keep rule as encoded:** nested clone reapable only when fully clean AND HEAD == live remote tip; scratch tree reapable only with zero keep-set files outside bulk subtrees (keep suffixes .md/.txt/.sh/.py/.ts/.js/.json/.yaml/.yml/.toml/.log; bulk = target, dist, node_modules, .git, cache, .cache, vendor, .bun, .npm, .venv, __pycache__); registered worktrees excluded (registration merged from every primary under ~/git); ≥4h idle gate for entries, 48h for targets; claimed task/issue, open PR, and live-process cwd gates re-verified fresh per removal — a tripped gate stops the run, never skips ahead. Whole entries move to recoverable trash `~/.local/share/Trash/yard-reaper/<run-id>/`, named one by one. Hard examination holds: `7780-1931-slice1` and `11081` (both verified present and untouched after every pass).

**Schedule (verified):** `yard-reaper.timer` enabled + active, hourly. Proof: the 17:08 CST timer fire started a real run on its own (it refused safely — see below), next trigger 18:07 CST. `cargo-target-janitor.timer` disabled by the install.

**Runs so far:**
- Dry run `yard-run-20261108T221134Z`: 1,469 entries classified — 404 eligible (scratch, no keep-set, 0.31 GiB total), 1,010 holds-keep-set, ~55 active-within-4h, examination holds excluded by name. Target plan selected 0 (the janitor's own run had just enforced the cap; 73.7 GB of targets remain, under the 150 GiB cap).
- First bounded apply `yard-run-20261108T222041Z` (cap 25): 25 entries reaped to trash (4,599,808 B), 379 deferred, no refusals, no errors.
- systemd-path apply `yard-run-20261108T223133Z`: 100 entries reaped to trash (11,481,088 B), 279 deferred. Total across passes: **125 entries, ~16 MB** — the eligible class is genuinely tiny probe dirs (Oct 27–31). The hourly runs drain the remaining 279.
- Timer-fired run `yard-run-20261108T230816Z`: **refused, exit 2, zero reaped** — the GitHub fallback for claimed issues (`gh api ... labels=queue/claimed`) returned non-zero (the laptop's user gh identity is under GitHub's secondary rate limit, hit repeatedly today). Fail-closed worked as designed: nothing was reaped on an unverifiable gate. Recorded here rather than hidden: when the rate limit clears, scheduled runs proceed; the broker claimed-ids source is unaffected.

**Yard size:** 294,742,306,816 B (274.50 GiB) fresh du before the passes; 205,045,211,136 B (190.97 GiB) measured as the 22:31Z run completed (the last few reaps after the measure were ~MBs of probe dirs). Attribution, honestly: the yard-reaper's own new-scope yield today is ~16 MB — the drop is dominated by the sibling worktree-reaper's concurrent runs (~169 GB today) plus normal fleet churn. The morning's 565 GB figure predates those reaps. Of the 274.50 GiB, 164.73 GiB is accounted by targets + non-target entries; the remainder is registered-worktree working files (the worktree-reaper's domain). The yard's bulk is live/registered work and keep-set material, not unexamined garbage.

**Held set (by name, with reasons):** `7780-1931-slice1` + `11081` — hard examination holds, untouched. 1,010 entries — keep-set files present (authored text/scripts/logs; e.g. `1627-scratch` with prove.sh/proof.txt/server.log, `watcher-bench-195` with 5 harness logs in results/, unregistered task dirs with repo/ checkouts whose heads were not proven equal to the live remote tip). ~55 entries — active within the 4h gate at scan time. Registered worktrees — the worktree-reaper's domain, excluded by design.

**Queue task 12665:** still `queued` in repo-health-code-pilot. The repo-queue claim verb takes the queue head (priority order), not a task id — verified live: a claim attempt took the head task instead, and completion/checkpoint verbs require a live claim by the worker identity. There is no verb to claim or complete a specific queued task out of order, so the row cannot be honestly flipped from here; this comment is the completion evidence, and the task's linked issue closing is the signal the queue's own reconciliation consumes. (The accidental head-task claim during this probing was cancelled immediately; no other task was touched.)

Run logs: `~/.local/state/yard-reaper/runs/` on the laptop. Closing: the reaper is built, merged, installed, on an hourly timer, has completed two apply passes, and its fail-closed refusal path is proven live.
